blocks.text: GIA is a private AI workspace that runs on your Android device or in the browser. There is no account to create and no cloud backend.
To use cloud models, open Settings → Engine Room and connect a provider with your own API key. To go fully on-device, enable On-Device Mode and load a local model in Settings → Local LLM.

items: Download the APK from GitHub Releases (Android) or open the Web app.
Connect a provider, or enable On-Device Mode for zero-key use.
Start chatting — GIA remembers what you tell it across modules.

blocks.text: The core workspace. Talk to GIA with tools, files, memory, and real-time streaming.

items: Attach files, images, or share from another app. Long pasted text is auto-wrapped as a .txt attachment.
GIA streams responses token-by-token and runs tools in a loop. Tool runs render as visual cards with live status.
Every response is tagged on-device or cloud so you always know where it ran.
Tap the provider pill in the chat header to switch model, thinking, and per-provider image model.
The 🔧 All Tools button opens the full tool catalog — tap any tool to copy its ID, then ask GIA to use it.

blocks.text: Built for students. Generate WASSCE and BECE quizzes, walk through past questions, and get instant feedback.

items: Create a practice quiz from a topic or past paper.
Step-by-step solutions with hints before answers.
Track what you have and have not mastered.

blocks.text: Turn raw data into clear, structured insight with charts and JSON-ready analysis.

items: Upload documents and query them with on-device RAG.
Produce charts and reports rendered inline.
Persistent memory of your metrics and goals.

blocks.text: Long-form and visual content — drafts, documents, slides, and code — generated and rendered inline. Files can be exported as PDF, DOCX, PPTX, or ZIP and previewed in the app.
Break big goals into calm, actionable steps — a study week, a project plan, or a personal roadmap.
Build autonomous agents with their own memory and RAG. Delegate work and oversee the result.

items: Define an agent with a name, role, instructions, and a per-agent tool grant (pick any of the 200+ registered tools).
Each agent gets per-agent retrieval over your files.
Mention agents inline with @Name to route a task.
GIA can delegate sub-tasks to agents via sub_agent_call and reads back their output.

blocks.text: Set a goal and let GIA drive toward it — planning, executing, and adapting without hand-holding.

GIA has 200+ registered tools: web search & browsing, code execution, terminal, files, PDF/DOCX generation, tasks & to-dos, security scanning, SSH, databases, smart home, MCP servers, plugins, image generation, maps, and more.

items: GIA calls tools by emitting ```tool blocks with a registered tool ID and JSON args.
Tool runs show live status cards with elapsed time, results, and errors.
Visual blocks render charts, maps (OpenStreetMap + live OSRM routing), 3D scenes, mind maps, and widgets inline in chat.
The full catalog is one tap away in chat (🔧 All Tools) and per-agent in Agents.

blocks.text: Skills are packaged instructions that shape how GIA handles a task. GIA ships with built-in skills and can install community skills from the Skills Marketplace (Settings → Skills).

items: GIA can list and switch skills itself via skill_list and skill_activate.
The active skill shows as a chip in the chat header.
Community skills come from SkillsMP, Anthropic's official skill collection, and the davila7 Claude templates registry.
Users can publish skills to the community via the landing page or the marketplace sources.

blocks.text: GIA supports voice input, text-to-speech, and a wake word.

items: Without a key, GIA uses its built-in on-device recognizer — the wake word works while the app is open.
Adding a free Picovoice access key enables the always-on native wake word engine.
Model Voice: with OpenAI or Gemini connected, GIA can read answers in the model's own native voice (OpenAI audio/speech, Gemini TTS) instead of the device voice — toggle it in Settings → Voice.
Configure voice settings under Settings → Voice.

blocks.text: On-Device Mode prefers the local LLM for every response when a model is loaded. Memory, embeddings, and translation run locally — nothing leaves your device.

items: Enable in Settings → Reliability → On-Device Mode.
Load a model in Settings → Local LLM (downloads via CDN).
If the local model is not ready, GIA falls back to your cloud provider and tags the response accordingly.

blocks.text: GIA has no cloud backend and no telemetry. Your data stays on your device unless you explicitly choose a cloud model.

items: No account, no tracking, no server-side logs.
API keys are stored locally and never sent to GIA servers.
Input guardrails block prompt injection and dangerous commands.
Security tools (security_scan, security_firewall, security_threat_intel) are built in.
No provider connected? Connect one in Settings → Engine Room, or enable On-Device Mode with the local Qwen LLM (zero key).
Image generation needs a provider that supports an images endpoint — set the image model in the chat header's Model & Provider sheet.
Terminal commands hang? The Android build includes a fix for the process-exit race — rebuild the APK from GitHub Actions.
Agent file uploads index on-device; the first index after a failed model load falls back to fast keyword search automatically.
